findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found, permission-denied, or I/O errors
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed IoError
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? to propagate the error from fs::read_to_string

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec by unchecked index after collect()-ing split results; malformed lines with zero commas cause a panic
findings.failure_mode: malformed input line (no comma) produces a Vec of length 1, and parts[0] panics or silently skips data
findings.fix: replace split+collect+indexing with split_once(',') and match the Some((left, right)) / None branches, returning a typed parse error on None

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the Vec by unchecked index; lines with only one field cause a panic
findings.failure_mode: malformed input line (missing second comma-separated field) triggers index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and destructure into left/right parts; access second element only via the matched pair

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range string in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: corrupt or adversarial data in the value column aborts the session loader instead of returning a ParseError
findings.fix: replace .unwrap() with ? (propagating through a Result return type) or map_err to a domain ParseError

findings.problem: 'as u16' silently truncates u32 values > 65535 with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value of 70000 silently becomes 4425, silently corrupting domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and propagate the error with ? or map_err to a domain OverflowError

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec of Strings only to index into it; split_once is the prescribed pattern
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation and heap pressure on every line; also invites unchecked indexing bugs
findings.fix: replace with line.split_once(',') and handle left/right directly without collect

findings.problem: println! inside load_sessions is a hidden I/O side effect in a data-loading function; callers cannot suppress or test it
findings.failure_mode: logging is baked into the data-loading path, making the function impossible to compose without stdout pollution and preventing test isolation
findings.fix: remove the println!; pass a logger or callback abstraction from the shell layer, or make logging a separate shell-only concern

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, domain construction, and console logging in a single public function with no clear boundary
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing and domain logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation from file system and stdout side effects
findings.fix: split into (1) a pure fn parse_session_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for the core, and (2) an imperative shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> that reads the file, delegates to parse_session_line, and handles logging at the shell layer

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 instead of typed domain newtypes (e.g., SessionName, SessionValue)
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct Record with invalid names or values that the domain rules should forbid at compile time
findings.fix: introduce newtype wrappers with fallible constructors that encode domain invariants, e.g., SessionName(String) with validation in try_from

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler or allocation analysis evidence
no second-ring evidence (no rayon/smallvec/cow decisions to justify)
no command evidence: cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy not run
no tests exist for the crate
residual_risk: High. All six Holzman BLOCKER rules are violated: unwrap on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, split+collect+index anti-pattern, hidden println! side effect, and no functional-core/shell boundary. The code is a single 23-line function that panics on any malformed input, silently truncates values, allocates unnecessarily, and cannot be tested in isolation. Static review only; no commands run. The crate requires a full rewrite to a typed, Result-returning, pure-core design before any delivery gate.
